text: Every determinism mechanism is named singly, and the mechanisms are named CORRECTLY for the artifact being graded. THIS ROW ASSERTED A FALSEHOOD UNTIL 2026-09-09 and the correction is snorkeltoast's, verified at the artifact by vc: the row said crawl determinism comes from --virtual-time-budget alone and that --force-prefers-reduced-motion does nothing to the crawl. THAT IS BACKWARDS FOR BUILD 008. player.html's reduced-motion block carries the rule `.crawl .text{animation:none!important}` -- cited by token -- and that rule IS the crawl fix. Its own comment records the measurement: the outro crawl went from RMSE 4.99 / 8.28 / 10.65 between captures to 0.000000 three times, and the comment states that the block previously claimed to drop all motion while naming .crawl zero times. Virtual time alone did NOT make the crawl deterministic; that is where slide 20's 12.45 came from. THE ROW WAS TRUE OF BUILD 007 AND THE FIX FALSIFIED IT, which is the hazard being recorded: a criterion describing a mechanism goes stale when the mechanism is repaired, and it goes stale SILENTLY because a row is prose and prose does not fail. The single-point-of-failure concern the row was minted for survives unchanged and is now the whole of it -- one mechanism described as two reads as covered when it is not. Discharged when the harness names each mechanism singly AND the naming is checked against the artifact it grades rather than against the build the row was written from.

state.evidence: FIXED AT snorkeltoast 186af24 AND VERIFIED BY vc AT THE SOURCE -- one paragraph, ten inserted lines, one file, no code change, which is the right size for a row about naming. shoot()'s docstring previously named both flags and left which-does-what to inference. It now states the division outright: VIRTUAL TIME FIXES WHEN THE FRAME IS TAKEN, REDUCED MOTION FIXES WHETHER ANYTHING IS STILL MOVING WHEN IT IS, and neither is redundant. It carries slide 20's 4.99 / 8.28 / 10.65 / 12.45 as the evidence that they are not interchangeable, and it records that until the crawl fix the player's reduced-motion block named .crawl zero times, so a rising crawl kept animating and virtual time alone did not settle it. THE DOCSTRING NAMES THE ERROR A READER WOULD MAKE FROM ITS OWN PREVIOUS TEXT, in those words -- caveat at production rather than at report, applied to a docstring. AND THE REASON THIS ROW WAS WORTH BUILDING IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, which is snorkeltoast's test and the best form of it produced in this thread: A READER WAS OBSERVED MAKING THE ERROR. That reader was vc, working carefully, which is what put the falsehood into this row in the first place; and cc will read the same lines to port capture in WP-03, so the next reader is named and imminent. A measured reader making a measured error is the scope test PASSING. Contrast AC-2.12, where the reader who would use a recorded host machine was measured NOT to exist, and the same test fails. Same test, opposite answers, and the difference is a reader rather than a judgement about cost.
